```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

# Package versions are pinned via renv (see renv.lock); run renv::restore() to install.
# Functions are called with explicit pkg:: prefixes rather than attaching via library().

# Headline numbers used in the Summary. The price shock is written by the export-price-shock
# chunk below; the land-use results by r/land_use_model/03_summarise_results.R.
shock_2035 <- utils::read.csv(file.path("data", "derived", "vegetable_oil_price_shock_2035.csv"))
lum <- utils::read.csv(file.path("data", "derived", "land_use_country_results.csv.gz"))

# Soybean oil's share of soybean crush value (Janzen & Wang 2025; see Methods). Must match
# SOY_OIL_VALUE_SHARE in r/land_use_model/01_prepare_data.R.
soy_oil_value_share <- 4.72 / (4.72 + 8.66)

# Additional forest loss relative to BAU: BAU stock minus scenario stock, so positive = more loss.
bau <- lum |>
  dplyr::filter(scenario == "bau") |>
  dplyr::select(country, year, carbon_bau = forest_carbon_tco2, area_bau = forest_area_ha)
loss <- lum |>
  dplyr::filter(scenario %in% c("vo_central", "vo_high", "vo_central_palm", "vo_central_soy")) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(bau, by = c("country", "year")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    carbon_loss = carbon_bau - forest_carbon_tco2, # t CO2
    area_loss = area_bau - forest_area_ha # ha
  )
global_loss <- loss |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    dplyr::across(c(carbon_loss, area_loss, carbon_bau, area_bau), sum),
    .by = c(scenario, year)
  )
gl <- function(scn, yr, var) global_loss[[var]][global_loss$scenario == scn & global_loss$year == yr]

final_year <- max(lum$year)
n_years <- final_year - min(lum$year)
country_final <- loss |>
  dplyr::filter(year == final_year) |>
  dplyr::mutate(share = carbon_loss / sum(carbon_loss), .by = scenario) |>
  dplyr::arrange(scenario, dplyr::desc(carbon_loss))
central_final <- country_final |> dplyr::filter(scenario == "vo_central")
# Countries whose additional loss peaks and then narrows by >5% (BAU later clears some of the
# same forest), among those with more than 1 Mt CO2 of additional loss.
gap_peaks <- loss |>
  dplyr::filter(scenario == "vo_central") |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    peak = max(carbon_loss),
    peak_year = year[which.max(carbon_loss)],
    final = carbon_loss[year == final_year],
    .by = country
  )
n_narrowing <- sum(gap_peaks$peak > 1e6 & gap_peaks$final < 0.95 * gap_peaks$peak)
mys <- gap_peaks[gap_peaks$country == "Malaysia", ]

# Crop attribution: palm-only and soy-only runs of the central shock. They sum to the joint run
# to within the interaction term reported here.
crop_split <- c(
  palm = gl("vo_central_palm", final_year, "carbon_loss"),
  soy = gl("vo_central_soy", final_year, "carbon_loss")
)
interaction_pct <- 100 * (gl("vo_central", final_year, "carbon_loss") - sum(crop_split)) /
  gl("vo_central", final_year, "carbon_loss")

fmt1 <- function(x) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 1, big.mark = ",")
fmt0 <- function(x) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 0, big.mark = ",")

# Figures: one ggplot2 theme and one set of colors throughout. Scenarios and crops keep the same
# colors in every figure; magnitude on maps uses a single-hue blue ramp.
col_surface <- "#fcfcfb"
col_land <- "#ecebe6"
col_scenario <- c(Central = "#2a78d6", Sensitivity = "#eb6834")
col_crop <- c("Oil palm" = "#1baf7a", "Soybeans" = "#eda100")
blue_ramp <- c("#cde2fb", "#9ec5f4", "#6da7ec", "#3987e5", "#256abf", "#184f95", "#0d366b")

theme_report <- function() {
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    ggplot2::theme(
      plot.background = ggplot2::element_rect(fill = col_surface, colour = NA),
      panel.grid.major = ggplot2::element_line(colour = "#e1e0d9", linewidth = 0.3),
      panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank(),
      text = ggplot2::element_text(colour = "#52514e"),
      axis.text = ggplot2::element_text(colour = "#52514e"),
      plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(colour = "#0b0b0b", face = "bold"),
      plot.title.position = "plot",
      legend.position = "top",
      legend.justification = "left"
    )
}
theme_map <- function() {
  theme_report() +
    ggplot2::theme(
      panel.grid.major = ggplot2::element_blank(),
      axis.text = ggplot2::element_blank(),
      axis.title = ggplot2::element_blank(),
      legend.position = "bottom",
      legend.justification = "center"
    )
}

# Country outlines (Natural Earth 1:110m), as vertices; see r/make_basemap.R.
basemap <- utils::read.csv(file.path("data", "natural_earth", "ne_110m_admin_0_countries.csv.gz"))
```

## Summary

All results are exploratory and preliminary.

- **Demand.** Meeting the Net-Zero Framework's Base target at least cost could require `r fmt0(shock_2035$vo_demand_billion_liters)` billion liters of virgin vegetable oil a year for marine renewable diesel by 2035 [@seber2025], equal to `r fmt0(shock_2035$demand_share_pct)`% of current world production of the four major vegetable oils.
- **Price shock.** Using elasticities from @chen2026, that demand raises vegetable-oil prices by about `r fmt0(shock_2035$pct_delta_p_central)`%; with those from @roberts2013, by `r fmt0(shock_2035$pct_delta_p_high)`%. A demand shift this large is far outside the range where constant elasticities are reliable, so read these as "prices rise to a multiple of baseline", not as point estimates.
- **Deforestation.** Raising palm oil prices `r fmt0(shock_2035$pct_delta_p_central)`% and soybean prices `r fmt0(soy_oil_value_share * shock_2035$pct_delta_p_central)`% in emLab's land-use model adds `r fmt1(gl("vo_central", 2035, "carbon_loss") / 1e9)` Gt CO₂ of forest carbon loss (`r fmt1(gl("vo_central", 2035, "area_loss") / 1e6)` Mha) over business as usual within 15 years, and `r fmt1(gl("vo_central", final_year, "carbon_loss") / 1e9)` Gt CO₂ (`r fmt1(gl("vo_central", final_year, "area_loss") / 1e6)` Mha) over the model's `r n_years`-year horizon. The Roberts & Schlenker shock gives `r fmt1(gl("vo_high", final_year, "carbon_loss") / 1e9)` Gt CO₂.
- **Where.** The loss is concentrated: `r central_final$country[1]` and `r central_final$country[2]` account for `r fmt0(100 * sum(central_final$share[1:2]))`% of it, and the top 12 countries for `r fmt0(100 * sum(central_final$share[1:12]))`%. The palm price shock drives `r fmt0(100 * crop_split[["palm"]] / sum(crop_split))`% of the loss and the soybean shock `r fmt0(100 * crop_split[["soy"]] / sum(crop_split))`%.
- **Next.** Converting this loss into an ILUC carbon intensity (g CO₂e/MJ), comparable to the 62 g CO₂e/MJ ICCT has used [@sturrup2026] and the 84.1 g CO₂e/MJ that @chen2026 estimate for palm, is the next step.

## Background

**The IMO Net-Zero Framework.** In April 2025 the International Maritime Organization approved draft amendments to MARPOL Annex VI that would set binding greenhouse-gas fuel-intensity (GFI) targets for ships of 5,000 gross tonnage and above, measured in well-to-wake g CO₂e/MJ against a 2008 baseline of 93.3 g CO₂e/MJ [@seber2025; @sturrup2026]. The Base target tightens from a 4% reduction in 2028 to 30% by 2035; the stricter Direct Compliance target from 17% to 43%. Ships above the Base target pay \$380/t CO₂e (Tier 2) on the excess; ships between the two targets pay \$100/t CO₂e (Tier 1). Adoption was delayed by at least a year from October 2025.

**Why it drives vegetable-oil demand.** Fuels are judged only on their life-cycle GFI, with no land-use-change safeguards. Blending a biofuel is cheaper than the \$380/t Tier 2 penalty, so the least-cost strategy is to blend just enough to meet the Base target. ICCT finds the cheapest option, used-cooking-oil renewable diesel (UCO-RD), is limited to about 5% of shipping energy, so virgin vegetable-oil renewable diesel (VO-RD) fills the gap, reaching 46% of shipping energy by 2035 [@seber2025].

| Fuel | Life-cycle carbon intensity (g CO₂e/MJ) |
|---|---|
| 2008 baseline | 93.3 |
| Heavy fuel oil (HFO) | 92.8 |
| Fossil LNG | 85.7 |
| Soy vegetable-oil renewable diesel (VO-RD) | 42.3 |
| Soy FAME biodiesel | 35.7 |
| Used-cooking-oil renewable diesel (UCO-RD) | 13.1 |

: Direct life-cycle carbon intensities used by ICCT [@seber2025]. None include indirect land-use change.

**Why ILUC matters.** Indirect land-use change (ILUC) happens when biofuel feedstock demand raises crop prices and higher prices push cropland into forest elsewhere. Those emissions sit outside the fuel's supply chain, so a fuel mix that complies on paper can carry large uncounted emissions. This analysis traces that chain:

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  A["IMO Net-Zero Framework"] --> F["Marine VO-RD demand<br/><i>ICCT cost-optimization</i>"]
  F --> B["Virgin vegetable-oil demand<br/><i>1.22 kg oil per kg RD</i>"]
  B --> C["Vegetable-oil price shock<br/><i>this report</i>"]
  C --> D["Forest loss by country<br/><i>emLab land-use model</i>"]
  D --> E["ILUC carbon intensity<br/><i>next step</i>"]
```

**Prior estimates.** Published ILUC values for vegetable-oil biofuels span more than an order of magnitude:

| Source | Approach | ILUC result |
|---|---|---|
| ICCT climate & revenue brief [@sturrup2026] | Fixed factor applied to ICCT's demand projection | 62 g CO₂e/MJ; ~285 Mt CO₂e/yr by 2035; ~950 Mt CO₂e over 2028–2035 |
| U.S. EPA model comparison [@epa2023mce] | Five models, 1 billion gal/yr soybean-oil biodiesel shock | 10 to 295 kg CO₂e/MMBTU (GCAM: 62) |
| @chen2026 | Econometric demand → price → deforestation chain for palm, 2002–2018 | 84.1 g CO₂e/MJ (90% CI 48.7–113.5) |
| GLOBIOM for the EU [@valin2015] | Global economic land-use model | > 100 g CO₂e/MJ for high-risk feedstocks |

: ICCT's 62 is the EPA's GCAM value, which the EPA reports in kg CO₂e/MMBTU (≈ 59 g CO₂e/MJ). With it, ICCT finds the ILUC-adjusted fleet GFI reaches 93.9 g CO₂e/MJ by 2035, above the fossil baseline [@sturrup2026].

Our design follows Chen et al.: estimate the price response to the demand shock, then let an econometric land-use model translate prices into forest loss, rather than assume an ILUC factor.

## Methods and assumptions

The analysis has four steps:

1. **Demand → price.** Convert ICCT's 2035 vegetable-oil demand into a vegetable-oil price shock.
2. **Price → model crops.** Map that shock onto the crop prices in emLab's land-use model.
3. **Prices → forest loss.** Simulate forest loss under baseline and shocked prices, at zero carbon price, and take the difference.
4. **Forest loss → ILUC intensity** (next). Divide the additional emissions by the fuel energy delivered.

### Demand → price shock {#sec-price-shock}

An outward demand shift moves the equilibrium price by the size of the shift divided by the gap between the supply and demand elasticities [@roberts2013]:

$$ \%\Delta P \;\approx\; \underbrace{\frac{D}{Q_0}}_{\text{demand shift}} \;\times\; \underbrace{\frac{1}{\varepsilon_s - \varepsilon_d}}_{\text{multiplier } M} $$

where $D$ is marine virgin vegetable-oil demand, $Q_0$ is baseline world production, $\varepsilon_s > 0$ is the supply elasticity and $\varepsilon_d < 0$ the demand elasticity.

| Input | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Marine virgin vegetable-oil demand, 2035 ($D$) | 139.3 billion L | ICCT [@seber2025], Table 1 |
| Baseline market ($Q_0$) | ≈ 204 Mt: world production of palm, soybean, rapeseed and sunflowerseed oil, 2024/25 | USDA PSD [@usdapsd] |
| Oil density, to put $D$ and $Q_0$ in the same units | 0.92 kg/L | ICCT's own soy-oil conversion: 12.4 Mt = 13.5 billion L (0.919 kg/L) [@seber2025], Table A1 |
| Demand elasticity, central ($\varepsilon_d$) | −0.284, the inverse of a demand flexibility of −3.523 (SE 1.085) | @chen2026, Table S1, col. 3 |
| Supply elasticity, central ($\varepsilon_s$) | ≈ 0.12: long-run 0.10 for palm and 0.13 for competing oil crops, weighted by production | @chen2026, Fig. 2B, rows 3–4 |
| Elasticities, sensitivity | $\varepsilon_s = 0.10$, $\varepsilon_d = -0.05$ | @roberts2013, Table 1 (ranges 0.09–0.12 and −0.03 to −0.07) |
| Demand year | 2035 only | Our choice: the final year of the ICCT projection |
| "Beyond marginal" flag | demand share > 25% | Our flag for where the approximation is unreliable; not from a source |

: Inputs to the price shock. The central multiplier is $M \approx 2.5$; the sensitivity, $M \approx 6.7$.

Notes on these choices:

- **Market definition.** Vegetable oils are close substitutes, so the shock plays out across the oil complex even though marine demand lands on soy [@chen2026]. $Q_0$ covers the same four oils as the Chen elasticities.
- **Supply elasticity stays in.** The land-use model takes prices as given, so the price it receives must already be an equilibrium price. Dropping $\varepsilon_s$ ($M \approx 3.5$) would overstate the shock by about 40%. This assumes the model's own supply response is broadly consistent with $\varepsilon_s \approx 0.12$; that is untested.
- **Large shocks.** The formula is a marginal approximation. From about 2032 marine demand is a large share of the market, where the true response is probably convex [@roberts2013], so the 2035 shock is indicative of scale only.
- **Long run.** Both elasticity sets are long-run values. Oil palm takes about four years to fruit, so short-run supply is nearly fixed [@chen2026].
- **Soy meal.** Crushing soybeans also yields meal, whose revenue partly offsets oil-price pressure; Roberts & Schlenker scale their effect by two-thirds when a third of the calories return as feed [@roberts2013]. We make no such adjustment to the oil-price shock, so it errs high. (Meal does enter how the shock reaches the model's soybean price; see below.)
- **Check.** The formula recovers both source papers' headline results (see [Results](#sec-results-price)).

### Price shock → the model's crops {#sec-mapping}

Following @chen2026, the same percentage shock applies to every vegetable-oil price. They price everything off palm, and show the four oil prices are cointegrated with near-unit long-run coefficients (soybean 1.04, canola 1.01, sunflower 0.86; their Table S5). Studies that model the oils as separate markets find partial, uneven transmission [@cui2017; @santeramo2017], so oil-specific pass-through is a possible refinement.

The land-use model has 17 crops. Only two are vegetable-oil crops: `Oil, palm`, priced per tonne of palm oil, and `Soybeans`, priced per tonne of whole beans. Upstream's code describes the model's baseline prices as observed 2020 prices: \$768/t for palm and \$415/t for soybeans. These are within about 2% of the World Bank's 2020 averages for palm oil (\$752/t) and soybeans (\$407/t), and far from soybean oil (\$838/t) [@worldbank2022pink]. The shock is mapped as follows:

| Model crop | Shock | Why | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Palm oil | $\%\Delta P$ | The model prices palm as oil | — |
| Soybeans | $s \times \%\Delta P$, with $s = 0.353$ | Oil is only part of a soybean's value; the meal price is held fixed. $s = \$4.72 / (\$4.72 + \$8.66)$, the 2007–2025 average per-bushel values of soybean oil and meal | @janzen2025 (USDA AMS Illinois plant prices; 11 lb oil and 48 lb meal per bushel) |
| Rapeseed/canola, sunflower | not modeled | Not among the model's crops | — |

: How the oil-price shock enters the land-use model.

- **Checks on $s$.** Irwin's 2007–2017 averages give 0.347 [@irwin2017]; World Bank 2020 prices for soybean oil and meal (\$838/t and \$394/t) give 0.33 [@worldbank2022pink]. The weekly share is volatile: 25–35% over 2013–2020, rarely below 35% since, and briefly 50% in 2021 and 2025 [@janzen2025]. This is an accounting pass-through, not an estimate of how soybean prices respond in the market.
- **Omitted crops.** Leaving out rapeseed and sunflower understates ILUC. We keep $Q_0$ over all four oils anyway, because the Chen elasticities are defined over that market; a two-oil $Q_0$ would enlarge the demand share and pair a four-oil elasticity with a two-oil quantity. In 2024/25 the six largest producers grew 86% of world rapeseed (Canada, EU, China, India, Australia, Russia) and 90% of sunflowerseed (Russia, Ukraine, EU, Argentina, Kazakhstan, China) [@usdapsd], which suggests the omitted response falls largely outside tropical forests. We have not quantified it.

### Prices → forest loss: the land-use model {#sec-land-use-model}

We use emLab's global deforestation model (`emlab-ucsb/land-based-solutions`), copied into this repository; [Appendix A](#sec-lum-changes) lists every change we made.

- **Estimation.** A fractional logit (fixest, quasibinomial) of each grid cell's annual deforestation share on agricultural revenue and remaining tree-cover share, with cell and country-by-year fixed effects, fit to 2001–2020 (29.1 million cell-years).
- **Revenue.** For each cell, the harvest-share-weighted sum over the 17 crops of (crop price minus a transport cost that scales with travel time to port and the crude-oil price) × attainable yield, capitalized at 5%.
- **Simulation.** Starting from 2020 tree cover, the fitted model runs forward one year at a time for 2021–2171 over 1,450,769 cells in 154 countries, with country effects held at their 2016–2020 average. Cleared forest does not regrow.
- **Scenarios.** Carbon price 0 throughout. **BAU** uses 2020 prices; **central** raises palm oil by `r fmt1(shock_2035$pct_delta_p_central)`% and soybeans by `r fmt1(soy_oil_value_share * shock_2035$pct_delta_p_central)`%; **sensitivity** raises them by `r fmt1(shock_2035$pct_delta_p_high)`% and `r fmt1(soy_oil_value_share * shock_2035$pct_delta_p_high)`%. Two more runs apply the central shock to each crop alone, to split the loss between palm and soybeans. Prices change permanently in the first model year, so model year 2035 means 15 years after the shock, not calendar 2035.
- **Outputs.** Forest carbon (t CO₂) is tree cover × carbon density; forest area (ha) is forest carbon ÷ carbon density, following the model's own conversion. Emissions are forest carbon lost: peat, soil carbon and foregone sequestration are not counted. As a check, modeled 2020 forest area is `r fmt0(sum(bau$area_bau[bau$year == 2020]) / 1e6)` Mha, `r fmt0(100 * sum(bau$area_bau[bau$year == 2020]) / 4.06e9)`% of FAO's 4.06 billion ha [@fao2020fra]; the two use different forest definitions.

### Forest loss → ILUC carbon intensity (next)

The planned last step divides cumulative additional emissions, annualized over the simulation horizon, by the annual energy of 2035 VO-RD use, giving g CO₂e/MJ that can be added to VO-RD's direct 42.3 g CO₂e/MJ [@seber2025]. Because the model resolves loss by cell, the intensity will decompose by country.

## Data

### ICCT demand projection

ICCT's Table 1 (p. 5) gives the least-cost fuel mix for 2028–2035 [@seber2025]. We scrape it from the PDF.

```{r}
#| label: scrape-icct-table-1

pdf_path <- file.path(
  "data",
  "icct_biofuel_demand_report",
  "ID-450-Vegetable-Oil_research-brief_final.pdf"
)

# Extract page 5 as text and keep only the data rows (years 2028–2035)
page5 <- pdftools::pdf_text(pdf_path)[5]
lines <- stringr::str_trim(stringr::str_split(page5, "\n")[[1]])
data_lines <- stringr::str_subset(lines, "^20(2[89]|3[0-5])\\b")

# Each data row yields exactly 10 numeric tokens:
#   year, shipping demand, base target, fossil LNG %,
#   UCO-RD %, UCO-RD bl, VO-RD %, VO-RD bl, UCO demand bl, VO demand bl
nums <- stringr::str_extract_all(data_lines, "[0-9]+\\.?[0-9]*")
mat <- do.call(rbind, lapply(nums, function(x) as.numeric(x[seq_len(10)])))

icct_table_1 <- tibble::as_tibble(mat, .name_repair = "minimal")
names(icct_table_1) <- c(
  "year",
  "shipping_energy_demand_ej",
  "base_target_trajectory_gco2e_mj",
  "fossil_lng_pct",
  "ucord_pct_energy_demand",
  "ucord_billion_liters",
  "vord_pct_energy_demand",
  "vord_billion_liters",
  "uco_demand_billion_liters",
  "vo_demand_billion_liters"
)

icct_table_1 <- icct_table_1 |>
  dplyr::mutate(year = as.integer(year)) |>
  dplyr::arrange(year)

knitr::kable(
  icct_table_1 |>
    dplyr::select(
      year,
      shipping_energy_demand_ej,
      base_target_trajectory_gco2e_mj,
      ucord_pct_energy_demand,
      vord_pct_energy_demand,
      vord_billion_liters,
      vo_demand_billion_liters
    ),
  col.names = c(
    "Year",
    "Shipping energy (EJ)",
    "Base target (g CO₂e/MJ)",
    "UCO-RD (% of energy)",
    "VO-RD (% of energy)",
    "VO-RD fuel (billion L)",
    "Virgin VO feedstock (billion L)"
  ),
  caption = "ICCT Table 1, selected columns [@seber2025]. Virgin vegetable-oil feedstock, the last column, is the demand shock D."
)
```

### Baseline vegetable-oil production

$Q_0$ is world production of the four oils in 2024/25, summed across countries from the USDA Foreign Agricultural Service's PSD oilseeds dataset (`data/usda_psd_oilseeds/psd_oilseeds_csv.zip`, retrieved 2026-07-31) [@usdapsd]. PSD estimates are revised continuously, so these differ slightly from the printed May 2025 circular [@usda2025oilseeds].

```{r}
#| label: psd-q0

psd_zip_path <- file.path("data", "usda_psd_oilseeds", "psd_oilseeds_csv.zip")
psd <- utils::read.csv(unz(psd_zip_path, "psd_oilseeds.csv"))

q0_market_year <- 2024 # marketing year 2024/25

psd_four_oils <- psd |>
  dplyr::filter(
    Commodity_Description %in%
      c("Oil, Palm", "Oil, Soybean", "Oil, Rapeseed", "Oil, Sunflowerseed"),
    Attribute_Description == "Production",
    Market_Year == q0_market_year
  ) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    production_mt = sum(Value) / 1000, # reported in 1000 MT
    .by = Commodity_Description
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(production_mt))

knitr::kable(
  psd_four_oils,
  digits = 1,
  col.names = c("Commodity", "World production, 2024/25 (million t)"),
  caption = paste0(
    "World production of the four major vegetable oils (USDA PSD). Total: ",
    round(sum(psd_four_oils$production_mt), 1),
    " million t."
  )
)
```

### Land-use model inputs and outputs

Model inputs are emLab's `land-based-solutions` data on Nextcloud (`data/parallelized/1_input/full`), read without modification. Simulation outputs (7 GB) stay out of the repository; `r/land_use_model/03_summarise_results.R` reduces them to country × scenario × year totals (`data/derived/land_use_country_results.csv.gz`) and 0.5° grid-square totals (`data/derived/land_use_grid_loss.csv.gz`), which this report reads. Map outlines are Natural Earth's 1:110m countries [@naturalearth], stored as plain coordinates by `r/make_basemap.R`.

## Results

### Vegetable-oil price shock {#sec-results-price}

```{r}
#| label: price-shock-parameters

# Q0: world production of the four oils (psd_four_oils), converted to billion liters at
# 0.92 kg/L, ICCT's own soy-oil conversion (12.4 Mt = 13.5 billion L, ICCT Table A1).
q0_mt <- sum(psd_four_oils$production_mt) # ~204 Mt
oil_density_kg_l <- 0.92
q0_billion_liters <- q0_mt / oil_density_kg_l # ~221 billion L

# Central elasticities (Chen et al. 2026). Demand: flexibility of -3.523 (Table S1 col 3)
# inverts to eps_d = -0.284. Supply: long-run 0.10 (palm) and 0.13 (competing oil crops)
# (Fig. 2B rows 3-4), weighted by production share as in their eps_S formula.
demand_flexibility_chen <- -3.523
eps_d_chen <- 1 / demand_flexibility_chen
share_palm <- psd_four_oils$production_mt[
  psd_four_oils$Commodity_Description == "Oil, Palm"
] /
  q0_mt
eps_s_chen <- 0.10 * share_palm + 0.13 * (1 - share_palm)

# Sensitivity: Roberts & Schlenker (2013) staple-food elasticities (Table 1).
eps_s_rs <- 0.10
eps_d_rs <- -0.05

# eps_d is negative, so the multiplier denominator is eps_s + |eps_d|.
m_chen <- 1 / (eps_s_chen - eps_d_chen) # ~2.5
m_rs <- 1 / (eps_s_rs - eps_d_rs) # ~6.7

# Check: each multiplier should recover its source paper's own headline price effect.
validation <- tibble::tribble(
  ~check                                                        , ~shock_pct , ~m     , ~reported                                  ,
  "Chen et al.: biofuels used 8.5% of vegetable oil, 2002-2018" , 8.5        , m_chen , "21.2% (90% CI: 12.2-28.5%)"               ,
  "Roberts & Schlenker: ethanol mandate = 5% of world calories" , 5.0        , m_rs   , "about 30% (5% x their multipliers: 29-39%)"
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(implied_pct = round(shock_pct * m, 1)) |>
  dplyr::select(check, shock_pct, implied_pct, reported)

knitr::kable(
  validation,
  col.names = c(
    "Check",
    "Demand shift (% of market)",
    "Implied %ΔP (our formula)",
    "Paper's result"
  ),
  caption = paste0(
    "Multipliers: central M = ", round(m_chen, 2), " (Chen et al.), sensitivity M = ",
    round(m_rs, 2), " (Roberts & Schlenker). Both recover their source's headline result."
  )
)
```

```{r}
#| label: derive-price-shock

# %ΔP_t = (D_t / Q0) * M, expressed as a percent. beyond_marginal flags years where the shift
# exceeds 25% of the market, outside the regime where the approximation is reliable.
price_shock <- icct_table_1 |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    year,
    vo_demand_billion_liters,
    demand_share_pct = 100 * vo_demand_billion_liters / q0_billion_liters,
    pct_delta_p_central = demand_share_pct * m_chen,
    pct_delta_p_high = demand_share_pct * m_rs,
    beyond_marginal = demand_share_pct > 25
  )

knitr::kable(
  price_shock |>
    dplyr::mutate(beyond_marginal = ifelse(beyond_marginal, "yes", "")),
  digits = 1,
  col.names = c(
    "Year",
    "VO demand (billion L)",
    "Share of market (%)",
    "%ΔP, central",
    "%ΔP, sensitivity",
    "Beyond marginal"
  ),
  caption = "Vegetable-oil price shock from marine biofuel demand. Rows flagged 'beyond marginal' indicate direction and scale only."
)
```

### Forest loss {#sec-results-forest}

Additional forest loss is BAU forest minus scenario forest, so it accumulates over time. The difference in the final year is the cumulative additional emissions over the whole horizon.

```{r}
#| label: forest-loss-global

horizons <- c(2035, 2050, final_year)
global_table <- global_loss |>
  dplyr::filter(year %in% horizons) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    years_after_shock = year - min(lum$year),
    carbon_gt = carbon_loss / 1e9,
    area_mha = area_loss / 1e6,
    pct_of_bau_carbon = 100 * carbon_loss / carbon_bau
  )

knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    "Years after shock" = global_table$years_after_shock[global_table$scenario == "vo_central"],
    "Central: Gt CO₂" = global_table$carbon_gt[global_table$scenario == "vo_central"],
    "Central: Mha" = global_table$area_mha[global_table$scenario == "vo_central"],
    "Central: % of BAU forest carbon" = global_table$pct_of_bau_carbon[global_table$scenario == "vo_central"],
    "Sensitivity: Gt CO₂" = global_table$carbon_gt[global_table$scenario == "vo_high"],
    "Sensitivity: Mha" = global_table$area_mha[global_table$scenario == "vo_high"],
    check.names = FALSE
  ),
  digits = 2,
  caption = "Cumulative additional forest loss relative to BAU, all countries."
)
```

```{r}
#| label: forest-loss-timeseries
#| fig-width: 7.5
#| fig-height: 4

global_ts <- global_loss |>
  dplyr::filter(scenario %in% c("vo_central", "vo_high")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    years_after_shock = year - min(lum$year),
    scenario = ifelse(scenario == "vo_central", "Central", "Sensitivity"),
    carbon_gt = carbon_loss / 1e9
  )

ggplot2::ggplot(global_ts, ggplot2::aes(years_after_shock, carbon_gt, colour = scenario)) +
  ggplot2::geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = col_scenario, labels = scenario_labels, name = NULL) +
  ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 150, 25), expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "Cumulative additional forest carbon loss relative to BAU",
    x = "Years after the price shock",
    y = expression("Gt CO"[2])
  ) +
  theme_report()
```

The effect arrives early but keeps growing: `r fmt0(100 * gl("vo_central", 2035, "carbon_loss") / gl("vo_central", final_year, "carbon_loss"))`% of the full-horizon central loss occurs within 15 years of the shock.

#### By country and crop

Running the central shock for each crop alone splits the loss by crop. Palm accounts for `r fmt0(100 * crop_split[["palm"]] / sum(crop_split))`% of it and soybeans for `r fmt0(100 * crop_split[["soy"]] / sum(crop_split))`%. The two single-crop runs add up to the joint run to within `r formatC(abs(interaction_pct), format = "f", digits = 2)`%, so the split is effectively additive.

```{r}
#| label: forest-loss-country-chart
#| fig-width: 7.5
#| fig-height: 5.2

top_n <- 12
top_countries <- central_final$country[seq_len(top_n)]
other_label <- sprintf("Other %d countries", sum(central_final$carbon_loss > 0) - top_n)

crop_by_country <- country_final |>
  dplyr::filter(scenario %in% c("vo_central_palm", "vo_central_soy")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    label = ifelse(country %in% top_countries, country, other_label),
    crop = ifelse(scenario == "vo_central_palm", "Oil palm", "Soybeans")
  ) |>
  dplyr::summarise(mt = sum(carbon_loss) / 1e6, .by = c(label, crop)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(label = factor(label, levels = rev(c(top_countries, other_label))))
bar_totals <- crop_by_country |> dplyr::summarise(mt = sum(mt), .by = label)

ggplot2::ggplot(crop_by_country, ggplot2::aes(mt, label)) +
  ggplot2::geom_col(
    ggplot2::aes(fill = crop),
    position = ggplot2::position_stack(reverse = TRUE), # palm first, from zero
    width = 0.62, colour = col_surface, linewidth = 0.4
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_text(data = bar_totals, ggplot2::aes(label = fmt0(mt)), hjust = -0.2, size = 3.2, colour = "#0b0b0b") +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = col_crop, name = NULL) +
  ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::label_comma(), expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "Additional forest carbon loss by country and crop",
    subtitle = "Central scenario, full horizon",
    x = expression("Mt CO"[2]),
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_report() +
  ggplot2::theme(panel.grid.major.y = ggplot2::element_blank())
```

```{r}
#| label: forest-loss-country-table

country_table <- country_final |>
  dplyr::filter(carbon_loss > 0) |>
  dplyr::select(country, scenario, carbon_loss, area_loss, area_bau, share)
by_scenario <- function(scn, ...) {
  country_table |> dplyr::filter(scenario == scn) |> dplyr::select(country, ...)
}
country_table <- by_scenario("vo_central", carbon_loss, area_loss, area_bau, share) |>
  dplyr::left_join(by_scenario("vo_central_palm", carbon_palm = carbon_loss), by = "country") |>
  dplyr::left_join(by_scenario("vo_central_soy", carbon_soy = carbon_loss), by = "country") |>
  dplyr::left_join(by_scenario("vo_high", carbon_high = carbon_loss), by = "country") |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    country,
    carbon_mt = carbon_loss / 1e6,
    palm_mt = dplyr::coalesce(carbon_palm, 0) / 1e6,
    soy_mt = dplyr::coalesce(carbon_soy, 0) / 1e6,
    area_kha = area_loss / 1e3,
    share_pct = 100 * share,
    pct_of_bau_area = 100 * area_loss / area_bau,
    carbon_mt_high = dplyr::coalesce(carbon_high, 0) / 1e6
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(carbon_mt))

DT::datatable(
  country_table,
  rownames = FALSE,
  colnames = c(
    "Country",
    "Central: Mt CO₂",
    "of which palm",
    "of which soybeans",
    "Central: thousand ha",
    "Central: share of total (%)",
    "Central: % of country's BAU forest",
    "Sensitivity: Mt CO₂"
  ),
  caption = "Cumulative additional forest loss relative to BAU over the full horizon, by country. Palm and soybean columns are the single-crop runs.",
  options = list(pageLength = 10, scrollX = TRUE)
) |>
  DT::formatRound(c("carbon_mt", "palm_mt", "soy_mt", "area_kha", "share_pct", "pct_of_bau_area", "carbon_mt_high"), digits = 1)
```

- **Concentration.** `r sum(central_final$carbon_loss > 0)` countries lose additional forest, but `r central_final$country[1]`, `r central_final$country[2]` and `r central_final$country[3]` account for `r fmt0(100 * sum(central_final$share[1:3]))`% of the full-horizon loss. Only cells whose harvest shares include oil palm or soybeans respond, since those are the only prices that change.
- **Some catch-up.** Cleared forest never regrows, so BAU can later clear forest the shocked scenario already cleared. In Malaysia additional loss peaks at `r fmt0(mys$peak / 1e6)` Mt CO₂ in model year `r mys$peak_year` and narrows to `r fmt0(mys$final / 1e6)` Mt CO₂ by `r final_year`; `r n_narrowing` countries narrow by more than 5% from their peak. Globally, additional loss is still growing at the end of the horizon. The ILUC step will need to treat this timing explicitly.

## Caveats and next steps

**Next steps**

- Convert the additional emissions into an ILUC carbon intensity (g CO₂e/MJ) and decompose it by country (stacked bar).
- Diff our model copy against upstream (snippet in `r/land_use_model/PROVENANCE.md`); the upstream team has refactored since our 31 July 2026 copy.

**What the estimates leave out or assume**

- **Forest carbon only.** Peat, soil carbon and foregone sequestration are not counted. In Chen et al., peat was 614 of 1,086 Tg CO₂e of net ILUC emissions [@chen2026], so this matters most for Indonesia and Malaysia. Understates.
- **Rapeseed and sunflower** are not in the model. Understates.
- **Price shock beyond the marginal regime.** The constant-elasticity formula is a local approximation; at a 63% demand share the true response is probably larger.
- **Soybean pass-through** is an accounting share (0.353), not an estimated market response.
- **No meal adjustment** to the oil-price shock. Overstates.
- **Supply-response consistency.** The price step assumes $\varepsilon_s \approx 0.12$; the land-use model's own supply response has not been checked against it.
- **Permanent shock from the first model year** and no forest regrowth, as described in [Methods](#sec-land-use-model).

## Appendix A: Changes to the land-use model code {#sec-lum-changes}

Every change made to the emLab land-use model to run the price-shock scenarios, listed for review by the model's authors. Starting point: upstream `emlab-ucsb/land-based-solutions`, `r/robert_test/parallelization/` at commit `e207c2b` (31 July 2026), copied to `r/land_use_model/` (see `r/land_use_model/PROVENANCE.md`). Anything not listed here is unchanged.

**Unchanged:** `simulation_functions.R` (including `update_revenues()` and `simulate_10_dt()`), `packages.R`, `r/directories.R` (now only read from, via `paths.R`), the deforestation model and its coefficients, and the fixed-effect construction (pixel FEs, the 2016–2020 country-year FE window, asymmetric-information FEs).

**All scripts**

1. `r/robert_test/parallelization/` → `r/land_use_model/` in every `here::here()` path.

**New file: `paths.R`**

2. Defines the input root `input_wdir`, read via `r/directories.R` as `{data_directory}/parallelized` and treated as read-only, and the output root `wdir`, the repo's git-ignored `land_use_model_runs/`. It stops if `wdir` is inside any Nextcloud folder or inside the inputs. This is so our outputs can't sync over the shared Nextcloud files of the same name.

**`01_prepare_data.R`**

3. Carbon price fixed at 0: `CP_LIST` (10 carbon prices) replaced by `CP <- 0`.
4. New input `PRICE_SHOCKS` (Section 1): % price change per shocked crop, one element per scenario, with `bau` first and unshocked. Scenarios: `bau`; `vo_20pct` (smoke test, `Oil, palm` and `Soybeans` both +20%); `vo_central` and `vo_high`, built from the 2035 shocks read from `data/derived/vegetable_oil_price_shock_2035.csv` (`pct_delta_p_central`, `pct_delta_p_high`), with `Oil, palm` taking the full shock and `Soybeans` taking `SOY_OIL_VALUE_SHARE` (0.353, Janzen & Wang 2025) of it; and `vo_central_palm` and `vo_central_soy`, the central shock applied to one crop at a time, for crop attribution. Sources for every number are in [Methods](#sec-mapping).
5. New Section 2b: expands `PRICE_SHOCKS` into `PRICE_SCENARIOS`, one full 17-crop price vector per scenario, starting from the `CPrice == 0` rows of `final_prices_allcp`. Writes `price_scenarios.csv`. Stops if a shocked crop isn't in the model, or if any crop in `endo_input_data` has no price.
6. Section 6: `update_revenues()` runs once per price scenario (`revenue_<scenario>` columns) instead of once per carbon price (`revenue_cp<P>`). BAU revenue is computed the same way instead of being taken from `data_past$revenue`, so every scenario uses one formula. The two BAU versions agree to ~1e-12, and the script prints that check on every run.
7. Section 8: chunk files carry `revenue_<scenario>` columns in place of `revenue_cp0` and `revenue_cp<P>`.
8. Section 8: the per-pixel attributes file `grid_smry.csv` also carries `lat` and `lon`, for mapping.
9. Section 11: `model_params.rds` stores `cp` and `price_scenarios` in place of `cp_list`.
10. Paths come from `paths.R` instead of the hard-coded `/Users/rheilmayr/Nextcloud/...` `wdir`, which upstream used for both inputs and outputs.

**`02_run_simulations.R`**

11. The 38 distinct simulations (56 labeled blocks across endog/exog, fi/fi_bl_vp/ai_bl_vp and carbon price) are replaced by one `simulate_10_dt()` run per price scenario, at `cp = 0` with `pixel_fe`. This is the same construction as upstream's `endog_fi_blvp` runs, $D(0, V(P))$, with scenario prices in place of carbon-price equilibrium prices.
12. Output parquet columns are `scn, pixel_id, year, biomass` (upstream: `crp_price, cprice, pixel_id, year, info, biomass`). The row-count check is now pixels × scenarios × years.
13. Paths come from `paths.R`, as in `01`.

**Disabled scripts**

14. `00_generate_sample_data.R`, `00c_run_cobweb.R`, `01b_prepare_uncertainty_draws.R`, `02b_run_simulations_uncertainty.R`, and `03_aggregate_results.R` through `09_conceptual_diagrams.R` (including `03b`) have a `stop()` as their first line. They still expect upstream's carbon-price outputs and use upstream's hard-coded paths, which on a colleague's machine point at the shared Nextcloud folder. `00` and `00c` write into `1_input/` itself. Each `stop()` comes out only when that script is adapted to `paths.R`.

**New file: `03_summarise_results.R`**

15. Reduces `02`'s per-pixel results to two files for the report, pairing each result file with its chunk file for each pixel's `country` and `CF`:
    - `data/derived/land_use_country_results.csv.gz`: country × scenario × year totals of forest carbon (`sum(biomass)`, t CO₂) and forest area (`sum(biomass / CF)`, ha, using upstream's `ha_per_pixel = CF_pix / CF`).
    - `data/derived/land_use_grid_loss.csv.gz`: per 0.5° grid square (from `grid_smry.csv` coordinates), 2020 forest carbon and final-year additional loss relative to BAU for each scenario.

    Stops if BAU 2020 forest carbon doesn't match `01`'s `grid_smry.csv`, or if any scenario's gridded loss doesn't sum to its country-level loss.

**`run_pipeline.R`**

16. `STAGES` runs `01` → `02` → `03_summarise_results.R`; upstream stages `03`–`07` are commented out.

**Verification** (200-pixel sample inputs, `1_input/smpl`):

- BAU emissions per pixel, annualized the same way as `03`'s `bl_emit_co2_y`, match upstream's reference run (`5_validation/sim_results_exog_ref_smpl.csv`) to within 0.003% for all 201 pixels.
- `vo_20pct` biomass is never higher than BAU, and is lower in the 110 of 201 pixels that grow palm or soy.

**Verification** (full inputs, `1_input/full`, 1,450,769 pixels):

- BAU revenue recomputed with `update_revenues()` matches upstream's `data_past$revenue` to within 7e-12.
- At every pixel, final-year (2171) biomass is never higher under a shock than under BAU, and never higher under `vo_high` than under `vo_central`. The shocks affect 711,420 pixels, those with a palm or soybean harvest share.
- `vo_central_palm` and `vo_central_soy` sum to `vo_central` to within 0.04% of its additional loss, 15 years after the shock and at the end of the horizon.
- `03_summarise_results.R`: BAU 2020 forest carbon summed by country equals `01`'s per-pixel 2020 biomass, and each scenario's gridded loss equals its country-level loss.
- Runtime on a 64 GB laptop, six scenarios: `01` 241 s (peak memory ~27 GB), `02` 145 s, `03_summarise_results.R` 43 s.
